# everpure_azure_volume (List Resource)

Lists the Volumes in a Volume Group, so they can be brought under Terraform with `terraform query`. Soft-deleted (destroyed, not yet eradicated) volumes are never listed: the `everpure_azure_volume` resource treats them as absent, so importing one would fail.

List resources require Terraform 1.14 or later, and importing the results by identity requires 1.12 or later. Results are sorted by `id`.

`terraform query -generate-config-out=<file>` writes an `import` block and a `resource` block for each result. `include_resource = true` additionally shows each result's attributes in the query output.

A `list` block returns at most 100 results by default and gives no warning when it stops there. Set the block's `limit` argument to raise the cap.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Save as discover.tfquery.hcl next to your configuration, then run
#   terraform query -generate-config-out=generated.tf
# to write an import block and a resource block for every volume found.

list "everpure_azure_volume" "all" {
  provider         = everpure
  include_resource = true

  config {
    volume_group_id = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east/volumeGroups/vg-prod-east"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group to list volumes in. Must be in the provider's own `subscription_id`.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `list` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when listing the volumes.
